Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-118.03850,34.13900.name: Harvest Fertility
-118.03850,34.13900.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Kathleen Kornafel, MD, PHD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

35.80204,31.77690.company: The Salk Institute for Biological Studies
35.80204,31.77690.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of The Salk Institute for Biological Studies. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-41.34442,-21.74588.name: Primordia Medicina Reprodutiva
-41.34442,-21.74588.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.clinicaprimordia.com.br. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

69.33000,41.34000.name: Center of Genomics and Bioinformatics
69.33000,41.34000.desc: Uzbekistan’s genomics institute, with cotton as its central crop. Uzbek cotton has been the subject of a long international campaign over forced labour in the harvest — so the same crop carries an engineering question and a labour question, and the second is the one that changed practice.
